title: Cristaux et cohomologie de De Rham : généralités, correspondances Deligne et Berthelot (1965-1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.), lettre (1965).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting. M and N are modules over a base ring R. The underlined M and N are the associated functors A ↦ M⊗_R A on R-algebras (Roby's 'lois polynômes'). Phi: M → N is a homogeneous polynomial law of degree n, i.e. a natural transformation of these functors.

Step 1, multihomogeneous components. Take x_1,…,x_r in M and indeterminates t_i. Expanding Phi(Σ t_i x_i) in N⊗R[t_1,…,t_r] gives
Phi(Σ t_i x_i) = Σ_{p_1+…+p_r=n} Phi_{p_1…p_r}(x_1,…,x_r) t_1^{p_1}…t_r^{p_r}.
This defines polynomial laws Phi_{p_1…p_r}: M^r → N, multihomogeneous of multidegree (p_1,…,p_r). Their values on R-points give set maps φ_{p_1…p_r}: M^r → N, defined for r ≥ 1, p_i ≥ 0, Σp_i = n.

Step 2, compatibility relations. Write each argument as a sum x_j = Σ_{1≤i≤s_j} x_{j,i}. Substitute independent indeterminates t_{j,i}, then specialise t_{j,i} → t_j. This yields
φ_{p_1…p_r}(Σ_i x_{1,i}, …, Σ_i x_{r,i}) = Σ φ_{q_{1,1},…,q_{r,s_r}}(x_{1,1},…,x_{r,s_r}),
the sum running over all splittings Σ_i q_{j,i} = p_j.

Step 3, reductions. The margin note says it suffices to impose the relation with a sum in only one argument, the others being single terms. To these one adds symmetry relations: permuting the arguments together with their indices.

Purpose. This is the start of a description of degree-n homogeneous polynomial laws as families of ordinary maps satisfying explicit identities. Equivalently, it presents Γ^n_R(M) (the degree-n divided powers) by generators x_1^{[p_1]}…x_r^{[p_r]} ↔ φ_{p_1…p_r}(x_1,…,x_r), so that Hom(Γ^n M, N) = Pol^n(M,N) (Roby's theorem). In the crystalline/divided-power context of this dossier, this is the kind of algebraic preliminary needed for divided powers of modules (Berthelot). The page breaks off at 'On suppose que l'on a … vérifiant …', presumably about to state the converse: such a family defines a polynomial law.

The neighbouring pages are unrelated typescript (a K-theory course announcement; Karoubi-style Clifford/Spin K-theory) used as scrap paper.
errors: The list of relations is incomplete for a converse characterisation: it lacks scalar homogeneity, φ_p(λ_1x_1,…,λ_rx_r) = λ_1^{p_1}…λ_r^{p_r} φ_p(x).
It also lacks the degeneracy relation that an argument with p_i = 0 can be deleted, φ_{…,0,…}(…,x_i,…) = φ_{…}(…) with x_i omitted. Only symmetry is announced as an extra.

Over a general base, reconstructing a polynomial law (a functor on all R-algebras) from the R-point maps φ needs this full set of relations (Roby's theorem / the presentation of Γ^n). The page does not reach the proof.
The degree 'n' is not written in the inserted 'de degré'; it is implicit from Σp_i = n.

ideas.what: Multihomogeneous components of a homogeneous polynomial law obtained by expanding Phi(Σ t_i x_i)
ideas.modern_name: Polarisation / multihomogeneous decomposition of polynomial laws
ideas.usually_credited_to: N. Roby (1963, 'Lois polynômes et lois formelles en théorie des modules')

ideas.what: Characterisation of degree-n polynomial laws by families φ_{p_1…p_r} subject to additivity-splitting and symmetry relations
ideas.modern_name: Presentation of Γ^n_R(M) by generators x_1^{[p_1]}…x_r^{[p_r]}; universal property Pol^n(M,N) = Hom(Γ^n M, N)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Roby 1963/1965; later Ferrand, Ziplies, Rydh (Γ^n via multihomogeneous presentations)
ideas.where_published: Roby 1963; Berthelot 'Cohomologie cristalline' (1974) uses Γ of modules

ideas.what: Reduction: it suffices to impose the splitting relation in one argument at a time
ideas.modern_name: Standard reduction of the additivity relations

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine sketch of Roby's theory of homogeneous polynomial laws and the presentation of divided powers Γ^n. It is a standard preliminary in the crystalline context. It is incomplete, and nothing here goes beyond Roby (1963).
transcription_corrections: First line: 'Une application polynomiale homogène' with 'de degré' added above the line; the 'n' is not actually written there.
In the relation, the left side reads φ_{p_1,…,p_r} with a Φ overwritten on it. The right side is φ_{q_{1,1},…,q_{r,s_r}}(x_{1,1},…,x_{r,s_r}), and the conditions are Σ_{1≤i_j≤s_j} q_{j,i_j} = p_j.
Margin note is plausibly: 'il suffit prendre un Σ dans un argument au plus, les autres termes réduits à un seul terme' (uncertain).
'Plus relations de symétrie' is an underlined heading.
